name: Cato Networks
product_focus: Cato SASE Cloud, Cato Socket, private backbone
evidence_summary: Cato sources evidence a cloud-native private backbone spanning 100+ PoPs and Private PoP option; SASE/SD-WAN is core platform positioning.
cost_model: Quote-based subscription; typically site/user/bandwidth/security bundle based.
key_differentiators: Single converged platform with no policy or log fragmentation across SD-WAN and security functions.
100+ PoP global private backbone reduces internet variability and provides predictable performance for SaaS-heavy traffic.
Strong story for organisations consolidating multiple point solutions onto one operational platform.
best_fit_for: Mid-market and enterprise buyers consolidating SD-WAN and SASE on one platform from a single vendor.
Global organisations with SaaS-heavy traffic patterns that benefit from a private backbone.
Teams without dedicated security operations capacity who want a managed SASE experience.
watch_outs: Less suited to best-of-breed buyers wanting Zscaler or Netskope as the SSE layer.
Customer does not own the underlay; circuits sourced separately, so multi-supplier coordination remains.
Less mature than incumbents for very large multinational deployments with heavy legacy MPLS estates.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason stated. Sources found and rejected are listed in the evidence register at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Real-time ML threat prevention, autonomous policy recommendations and built-in DEM.

resilience.note: Self-healing backbone; sockets fail over between PoPs automatically with no customer action.

profile.platform_architecture: Cato built SASE as a cloud service from day one: the Cato SASE Cloud runs on a private global backbone of 100+ PoPs connected by SLA-backed tier-1 carrier links, with thin Cato Socket edges at sites and a single-pass processing engine in every PoP. All traffic, site and remote user alike, is processed once in the nearest PoP under one policy. Orchestration is a single multi-tenant console with no separate controllers to run.
profile.security_sase: The full security stack is native and converged: NGFW, SWG, CASB, DLP, ZTNA, IPS and anti-malware execute in the same pass with shared context, and real-time machine learning models score traffic inline. There is no policy fragmentation between SD-WAN and security because they are one platform. Depth in specialist areas like enterprise DLP trails the dedicated leaders slightly; coherence across the whole stack is the compensating strength.
profile.service_support_channel: Cato sells direct and through partners with managed and co-managed options; UK channel presence has grown steadily and several MSPs wrap Cato with local support and underlay. Deployment speed is a signature: sites typically come online in hours once circuits exist. Support runs 24x7 from Cato with named success management on enterprise contracts.
profile.commercials_verdict: Subscription pricing per site bandwidth and per user for remote access, quote based and generally mid-market friendly. The Netify verdict: shortlist Cato when you want true single-vendor SASE with the least operational surface, global sites that need a predictable middle mile without MPLS, and a deployment measured in days. Buyers needing best-of-breed depth per security category or full underlay ownership should weigh the trade-offs.

vendor_faqs.q: What does the Cato private backbone actually give me?
vendor_faqs.a: Your traffic rides Cato's SLA-backed core between 100+ PoPs instead of the public internet middle mile, which stabilises latency and loss between regions, notably into and out of Asia and across the Atlantic, without buying MPLS.

vendor_faqs.q: How fast is a Cato deployment really?
vendor_faqs.a: Sockets are zero-touch: sites typically join the SASE Cloud in hours once connectivity exists, and remote users onboard with an agent in minutes. Policy build and migration planning remain the genuine project work.

vendor_faqs.q: Where does Cato fit against Zscaler or Netskope?
vendor_faqs.a: Cato converges SD-WAN and security in one cloud with one console; Zscaler and Netskope lead on specialist SSE depth and pair with third-party SD-WAN. Choose Cato for convergence and simplicity, the SSE leaders for category-deep security with a dual-vendor design.

shortlist_summary: Scored as easiest-to-use platform by Netify for the third year running, Cato offer a converged cloud-native SASE platform and is typically shortlisted by businesses needing to consolidate appliances or have limited in-house expertise to manage a SASE solution.
cost_note: Quote-based subscription, positioned mid-market: neither the cheapest nor the most expensive, with convergence reducing tool sprawl.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (Israel and US). Delivers in the UK from London and Manchester PoPs; contract direct or through UK partners including Netify routes.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Choose Cato or a partner for complete hands-free management.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Cato's own services page offers Hands-Free Management delivered either by Cato directly or by a partner, with "Expert staff perform every networking and security policy change as your needs evolve." Combined with Site Deployment, Intelligent Last-Mile Monitoring and MDR on the same page, Cato covers deploy, monitor, change and support end to end. Note the wording gives the customer a choice of Cato or partner as the operator.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: A co-management model across customer, partner, and Cato is available, and Cato always maintains the platform.
f03_co_managed_service.note: Explicit three-way co-management model stated on Cato's own services page, with Cato retaining platform operation. This matches the definition precisely: provider runs the platform, customer retains selected rights.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: True multi-tenancy and immediate access to new features and capabilities simplifies centralized management and enables partners to focus on delivering a great managed service experience.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Multi-tenancy and delegated partner administration are clearly evidenced via the MSASE Partner Platform, and the MSP page states "Strengthen Your Brand: Deliver a seamless, co-branded customer experience with the MSASE Partner Platform, reinforcing your brand identity at every touchpoint." However Cato's own wording is consistently "co-branding" and "co-branded", not white-label: "Everything from license management to co-branding is available in one place." Graded partial because the definition requires operation under the MSP's own brand, and no full white-label claim was found on the pages read.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: The zero-touch Cato Socket deploys quickly at your premises, by you, or with Cato and partner remote or on-site support.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Deployment assistance from Cato and partners, remote or on-site, is documented, and the same page adds "Each site is fully configured with the right networking, QoS, security, and failover policies." Graded partial rather than yes because the definition requires structured discovery, pilots, staging, migration runbooks, rollback plans and training, and none of those were named on any page reviewed. A Cato careers listing for a Professional Services Engineer was fetched but returned no usable job description text, so it is not relied on.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: No software for you to upgrade, patch, or otherwise maintain.
f07_lifecycle_management.note: Software upgrade and patching are unambiguously part of the service: the MSASE page adds "Autonomous Life Cycle Management: Cato ensures the SASE cloud platform maintains optimal security posture, 99.999% service availability, and low-latency security processing for all users and locations, without any customer involvement." and the Private PoP release adds "Cato manages the software lifecycle of the private PoP for service providers, including automated software updates and seamless deployment of new security patches and features." Graded partial because hardware replacement, RMA, renewals and end-of-life planning for the Socket were not found on any page reviewed.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Socket X1600 now has a hardware version that supports Cellular (LTE/5G) connections
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: Cato's own Learning Center documents integrated LTE/5G on the X1600 Socket, dual SIM management ("By default, SIM Slot 1 is the active one, while Slot 2 is standby.") and signal monitoring via RSSI, RSRP, SINR and RSRQ. The platform page corroborates transport choice: "Customers can choose any mix of fiber, cable, xDSL, and cellular connections." All three definition elements (transport, SIM management, signal monitoring) are met.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Cato Neural Edge powers the global cloud network through a dense footprint of 85+ physical Points of Presence (PoPs) hosted in top-tier regional datacenters and interconnected by multiple global and regional carriers.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: These are Cato's own PoPs running Cato's own software stack, not a third party's gateways resold, so yes rather than partner_integrated. The PoPs deliver security enforcement and remote access as a cloud service. The datacentre space and the interconnecting carriers are third party, but the gateway service itself is Cato's.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: Cato Private PoP enables service providers to maintain traffic locally, optimize network performance, and ensure security and compliance.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Cato Private PoP, announced 10 June 2025, places a dedicated PoP inside a service provider's own infrastructure. The same release states "Keep customer data local within the service provider's network infrastructure, addressing regional sovereignty and regulatory requirements." The offer is framed for service providers rather than for direct enterprise customers, which is worth checking in any specific deal.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Cato Neural Edge is a cloud-native, private global backbone spanning 100+ PoPs worldwide.
f21_private_global_backbone.note: Global rather than national, and controlled by Cato end to end.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: PoPs interconnect across multiple tier-1 providers, backed by SLAs on availability, latency, packet loss, and jitter.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Contractual rather than best-effort: the Master Service Agreement defines an SLA Metric of 99.999% availability with a tiered service level credit schedule (5%, 7% and 9% credits at defined availability bands) and a processing time commitment of 10 milliseconds for IPS, CASB and NGFW for Internet Access. Availability, latency, packet loss and jitter are all named. Change handling commitments as such were not found in the pages read.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: FWaaS controls traffic flow, across all ports and protocols, and in all directions both WAN (east-west), and the Internet (south-north).
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Native, not partner_integrated. The platform page states that the SSE 360 stack "converges the following capabilities: network segmentation and zero-trust (FWaaS), threat prevention (SWG, IPS, Malware Prevention, DNS Security, RBI), and application and data protection (CASB, DLP, ZTNA)", all built on Cato's own Single Pass Cloud Engine (SPACE) architecture and delivered from Cato PoPs rather than a separate appliance. Stateful firewalling, IPS, malware prevention, URL/web filtering and application control are all present in the one engine.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engine enforces access policies and granular actions on sensitive data across on-premises and cloud destinations from corporate and BYOD devices.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Native DLP inside SSE 360. The dedicated DLP page adds a catalog of 350+ pre-defined data types, custom data types based on Microsoft Information Protection labels, keywords and regular expressions, Exact Data Match, OCR scanning of image files, and a dedicated DLP events dashboard. Explicit exception workflow wording was not found, but classification, inspection, blocking and alerting are all evidenced.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: Cato monitors your last-mile ISPs 24×7 at every site.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: 24x7 proactive monitoring with incident ownership is evidenced: "On an outage or performance degradation, Cato works with the ISP to resolve it and keeps you informed, so teams that left managed MPLS don't burn IT resources chasing global ISPs." On the security side the MDR datasheet states "Customers can offload the process of detecting compromised endpoints to Cato's SOC team." and "Cato generates monthly custom reports, summarizing security posture, all detected threats, descriptions, risk levels, impacted endpoints, and more." plus "Assessment Check-Ups" reviews. Confidence is medium because the phrase root cause analysis and formal change governance wording were not found verbatim on any page read; the Cato support page carried no NOC, SOC, response time or escalation detail at all.

delivery_model.quote: Choose Cato or a partner for complete hands-free management.
delivery_model.note: Cato authors and owns the SASE platform and the SSE 360 security stack, and separately operates managed services itself (Hands-Free Management, MDR, Intelligent Last-Mile Monitoring, Site Deployment) while also enabling partners to deliver managed SASE through the MSASE Partner Platform. Both a technology vendor and a managed provider.

underlay_ownership.quote: Cato Neural Edge powers the global cloud network through a dense footprint of 85+ physical Points of Presence (PoPs) hosted in top-tier regional datacenters and interconnected by multiple global and regional carriers.
underlay_ownership.note: Cato owns and controls the PoP software, routing and the backbone as a logical network, but it does not own physical fibre. Core inter-PoP capacity is bought from third parties: "PoPs interconnect across multiple tier-1 providers, backed by SLAs on availability, latency, packet loss, and jitter." The last mile is customer-supplied: "Customers can choose any mix of fiber, cable, xDSL, and cellular connections." Graded mixed because it combines resold third-party transit with customer-supplied access, over Cato-owned routing. If the grading scheme requires a single strict reading of physical circuit ownership, resells_third_party_circuits would also be defensible.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Cato SASE Cloud Platform includes a cloud-native security stack, SSE 360.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Built by Cato, not licensed from another security vendor. The same page states the stack "is based on Cato's Single Pass Cloud Engine (SPACE) architecture and converges the following capabilities: network segmentation and zero-trust (FWaaS), threat prevention (SWG, IPS, Malware Prevention, DNS Security, RBI), and application and data protection (CASB, DLP, ZTNA)." No third-party security vendor is named as the underlying engine on any page reviewed. Cato is one of the few single-vendor SASE suppliers where the network and security layers are the same codebase.

regulatory_documentation.quote: Cato holds SOC2 and SOC3 certifications, which are independently validated by a third party.
regulatory_documentation.note: Named on the Cato compliance page: SOC 2 and SOC 3, PCI-DSS Level 1, ISO/IEC 27001:2013, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, ISO/IEC 27018:2019, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, ISO/IEC 14001:2015, UK Cyber Essentials, CSA STAR Self-Assessment, GDPR, and Esquema Nacional de Seguridad (ENS) High. NOT found on the pages reviewed: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2, FedRAMP and HIPAA. Note also that the CSA STAR entry is described as a Self-Assessment rather than a third party certification, and the ISO 27001 citation is against the superseded 2013 version rather than 2022.

pop_count.quote: Cato Neural Edge is a cloud-native, private global backbone spanning 100+ PoPs worldwide.
pop_count.note: Cato publishes two figures on this page. The body copy and stat tile state 100+ PoPs for Cato Neural Edge; the page's meta description still reads 85+ points of presence. The body figure is treated as current and the stale meta description is recorded rather than hidden.

sla_availability_pct.quote: Cato ensures the SASE cloud platform maintains optimal security posture, 99.999% service availability, and low-latency security processing for all users and locations, without any customer involvement.
sla_availability_pct.note: The figure is contractual, not just marketing: Cato's Master Service Agreement defines the SLA Metric or Service Level as the overall Availability metric of 99.999%, with service level credits of 5%, 7% and 9% at defined availability bands, plus a separate processing time commitment of 10 milliseconds for IPS, CASB and NGFW for Internet Access. The quote given is taken from the MSASE partner page because the MSA rendering contained formatting characters that would not reproduce cleanly.

conflicts.claim_a: The Cato Global Private Backbone is a private cloud-native network spanning 85+ points of presence (PoPs) worldwide.

Cato Neural Edge powers the global cloud network through a dense footprint of 85+ physical Points of Presence (PoPs) hosted in top-tier regional datacenters and interconnected by multiple global and regional carriers.
